content.text:
## Summary

I picked **Stripe** (Checkout + subscriptions + webhooks) — it's the standard for a Next.js app with no existing billing infrastructure, has a well-typed SDK, and its test mode makes local iteration easy.

**`src/lib/users.ts`** — extended `User` with `plan: "free" | "pro"` and an optional `stripeCustomerId`, plus `setUserPlan`, `setUserStripeCustomerId`, and `getUserByStripeCustomerId` helpers. Everyone starts on `free`.

**`src/lib/stripe.ts`** — lazy Stripe client (only throws if `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` is missing when a route actually needs it, not at build time).

**`src/lib/plans.ts`** — the Pro plan's Stripe Price ID (from env) and display info.

**`src/app/api/checkout/route.ts`** — `POST` handler the dashboard form submits to. Loads the current user, creates/reuses a Stripe Customer, opens a `subscription`-mode Checkout Session (with `client_reference_id`/`metadata` set to the user id so the webhook can find them), and 303-redirects to Stripe's hosted checkout page.

**`src/app/api/webhooks/stripe/route.ts`** — verifies the Stripe signature via `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, then on `checkout.session.completed` flips the user to `pro` (and records their Stripe customer id). Also handles `customer.subscription.updated`/`.deleted` to downgrade back to `free` if a subscription lapses or is canceled — same mechanism, so it seemed worth the few extra lines rather than leaving users stuck on "Pro" forever.

**`src/app/dashboard/page.tsx`** — shows the signed-in user's current plan, an "Upgrade to Pro — $12/mo" button (plain HTML form → `/api/checkout`, no client JS needed), and success/canceled/error banners driven by the `?checkout=` query param Stripe redirects back with.

**`.env.example`** — `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `STRIPE_PRICE_ID_PRO` placeholders with a note on getting real test values and using `stripe listen` locally. Had to add a `!.env.example` exception to `.gitignore` since it had a blanket `.env*` ignore rule that would've silently dropped the template too.

Verified: `npm run build` and `npm run lint` both pass, and I smoke-tested the routes against a running dev server (dashboard renders, checkout redirects to an error state gracefully when Stripe isn't configured, webhook correctly rejects unsigned requests).

**Not wired up** (would need real infra to matter here): there's no real session/auth in this app — `getCurrentUser()` just returns the first in-memory user, same as before — so checkout always acts on that user. Data is also still in-memory, so plan upgrades reset on server restart, matching how `users.ts` already worked.

## Summary

I picked **Stripe** (Checkout + subscriptions + webhooks) — it's the standard for a Next.js app with no existing billing infrastructure, has a well-typed SDK, and its test mode makes local iteration easy.

**`src/lib/users.ts`** — extended `User` with `plan: "free" | "pro"` and an optional `stripeCustomerId`, plus `setUserPlan`, `setUserStripeCustomerId`, and `getUserByStripeCustomerId` helpers. Everyone starts on `free`.

**`src/lib/stripe.ts`** — lazy Stripe client (only throws if `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` is missing when a route actually needs it, not at build time).

**`src/lib/plans.ts`** — the Pro plan's Stripe Price ID (from env) and display info.

**`src/app/api/checkout/route.ts`** — `POST` handler the dashboard form submits to. Loads the current user, creates/reuses a Stripe Customer, opens a `subscription`-mode Checkout Session (with `client_reference_id`/`metadata` set to the user id so the webhook can find them), and 303-redirects to Stripe's hosted checkout page.

**`src/app/api/webhooks/stripe/route.ts`** — verifies the Stripe signature via `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, then on `checkout.session.completed` flips the user to `pro` (and records their Stripe customer id). Also handles `customer.subscription.updated`/`.deleted` to downgrade back to `free` if a subscription lapses or is canceled — same mechanism, so it seemed worth the few extra lines rather than leaving users stuck on "Pro" forever.

**`src/app/dashboard/page.tsx`** — shows the signed-in user's current plan, an "Upgrade to Pro — $12/mo" button (plain HTML form → `/api/checkout`, no client JS needed), and success/canceled/error banners driven by the `?checkout=` query param Stripe redirects back with.

**`.env.example`** — `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `STRIPE_PRICE_ID_PRO` placeholders with a note on getting real test values and using `stripe listen` locally. Had to add a `!.env.example` exception to `.gitignore` since it had a blanket `.env*` ignore rule that would've silently dropped the template too.

Verified: `npm run build` and `npm run lint` both pass, and I smoke-tested the routes against a running dev server (dashboard renders, checkout redirects to an error state gracefully when Stripe isn't configured, webhook correctly rejects unsigned requests).

**Not wired up** (would need real infra to matter here): there's no real session/auth in this app — `getCurrentUser()` just returns the first in-memory user, same as before — so checkout always acts on that user. Data is also still in-memory, so plan upgrades reset on server restart, matching how `users.ts` already worked.
